review: Read full API, controller hook, room controls, view model, exact-room navigation helper and four test files. First-party React/browser orchestration and synthetic tests; no credentials, audio, personal profile payloads or third-party implementation exported.

The selected capacity profile is sent explicitly; default create does not silently select group voice. UI labels three-person voice as pending and distinguish consent readiness from installed group-media availability.

Room controls consume a bounded one-shot navigation hint after mounting, abort exact-room reads when superseded or account scope changes, and clear queued hints on account change. The hint is a navigation request, not room membership or action approval.

The new source dependency validates the supported room-ID shape and bounded environment reference, expires a pending hint after twelve seconds, and stores it only in module memory. The room controller must still perform the authenticated read.

The API uses same-origin credentialed no-store requests and encoded room paths; all server-side admission, consent and runtime funding remain authoritative. The hook type now accepts the existing three-person voice profile without adding media implementation.
The native panel receives the explicit mute-local-GPT callback. Existing controls retain separate host-transport invalidation, consent checks, room text owner state and owner-action callbacks.
limits: Unfrozen private source proposal; no canonical edits during this cohort, commit, deployment or publication.

Tests use synthetic room projections and mocked hooks/fetch. They do not qualify actual account transitions, hosted authorization, microphone consent, three-person audio, GPT Live or Minecraft continuity.
Controller-hook runtime operations and provider/mute callback effects are read and syntax-checked but not directly executed by these focused tests.
Shared contracts and other client/runtime modules are separate dependencies. Source preview is not a standalone application.
